title: ACCEPTANCE.json not among imported sources
description: ANALYSIS.md notes that ACCEPTANCE.json is cited by INSTRUCTIONS.md but was not imported. Story IDs were therefore preserved from the INSTRUCTIONS.md Governed Stage Boundaries list and from STORY_GUIDANCE.json.
system_choice: Use the ten story IDs from STORY_GUIDANCE.json unchanged and record the missing ACCEPTANCE.json as a disclosure.

title: Module path is a placeholder
description: The sources name github.com/owner/toml-decoder only as a sample module path.
system_choice: Use github.com/owner/toml-decoder as the module path because the sources name no other.

title: decoder-contract ordering is set by depends, not list position
description: The governed gate for decoder-contract decodes answer = 42 and rejects an unterminated array, so it requires parser-keys, parser-lexical-scalars, and parser-arrays-inline to exist first.
system_choice: Declare those three stories in depends so the Manifest orders decoder-contract after them, regardless of list position.

title: Stub Decode signature
description: Decode returns (map[string]any, error) and always returns ErrNotImplemented, so the command's JSON encoding path is wired and testable before the parser exists. The tagged-value model will replace map[string]any in a later block. Is that acceptable, or should the stub use a different shape?
system_choice: Decode returns (map[string]any, error) and always returns ErrNotImplemented, so the command's JSON encoding path is wired and testable before the parser exists. The tagged-value model will replace map[string]any in a later block. Is that acceptable, or should the stub use a different shape?

title: Exit status for command-line arguments
description: The spec requires that the decoder accept no arguments but does not name an exit code for rejecting them. I exit 2, the conventional usage-error code, with a diagnostic on stderr and nothing on stdout. Decode failures keep exit 1. Is 2 acceptable, or should arguments use 1 like other failures?
system_choice: The spec requires that the decoder accept no arguments but does not name an exit code for rejecting them. I exit 2, the conventional usage-error code, with a diagnostic on stderr and nothing on stdout. Decode failures keep exit 1. Is 2 acceptable, or should arguments use 1 like other failures?

title: Array encoding
description: Options were the tagged {"type":"array","value":[...]} form and a plain JSON array. I implemented a plain JSON array, as toml-test v2.2.0's JSON description and the arrays-round-trip criterion specify. Tagged form is for scalars only.
system_choice: Options were the tagged {"type":"array","value":[...]} form and a plain JSON array. I implemented a plain JSON array, as toml-test v2.2.0's JSON description and the arrays-round-trip criterion specify. Tagged form is for scalars only.

title: Earlier rejection tests
description: Two earlier-block tests asserted that arrays and inline tables are rejected. I moved the valid forms to positive tests and replaced them with malformed-array and malformed-inline-table cases. Confirm this is acceptable.
system_choice: Two earlier-block tests asserted that arrays and inline tables are rejected. I moved the valid forms to positive tests and replaced them with malformed-array and malformed-inline-table cases. Confirm this is acceptable.

title: Delimiter and offset letter case
description: Accepted lowercase t and z as well as T, Z and space, following the TOML ABNF's case-insensitive literals. The spec names only T or a space. Is that acceptable, or should lowercase be rejected?
system_choice: Accepted lowercase t and z as well as T, Z and space, following the TOML ABNF's case-insensitive literals. The spec names only T or a space. Is that acceptable, or should lowercase be rejected?

title: Fractional-second precision
description: Kept up to 9 fractional digits (nanosecond precision), truncating anything beyond, never rounding or padding. The spec does not name a precision. Is 9 digits acceptable?
system_choice: Kept up to 9 fractional digits (nanosecond precision), truncating anything beyond, never rounding or padding. The spec does not name a precision. Is 9 digits acceptable?

title: Internal representation of dotted-key tables
description: Nested tables are built with an internal table type that is distinct from tagged leaf maps, then exported as plain map[string]any. This keeps a table from being mistaken for a value when checking redefinition. Acceptable, or should the representation change on replan?
system_choice: Nested tables are built with an internal table type that is distinct from tagged leaf maps, then exported as plain map[string]any. This keeps a table from being mistaken for a value when checking redefinition. Acceptable, or should the representation change on replan?

title: Float output format
description: Finite floats are emitted with strconv 'g' shortest form (for example 1e6 becomes 1e+06). The spec does not fix a float string format, and the staged suite accepted this format. Is that acceptable, or should floats use a fixed notation?
system_choice: Finite floats are emitted with strconv 'g' shortest form (for example 1e6 becomes 1e+06). The spec does not fix a float string format, and the staged suite accepted this format. Is that acceptable, or should floats use a fixed notation?

title: Scoped suite pattern
description: The declared pattern uses '|' separators, which toml-test does not support. It selects 0 cases and exits 0. I verified the slice with the comma-separated equivalent (110 cases, all passing). The criterion's pattern should be corrected on replan.
system_choice: The declared pattern uses '|' separators, which toml-test does not support. It selects 0 cases and exits 0. I verified the slice with the comma-separated equivalent (110 cases, all passing). The criterion's pattern should be corrected on replan.

title: Dotted keys and table headers
description: Rejected as syntax errors in this block; only top-level key = string pairs are decoded. The string slice needs no more than that. Is that acceptable, or should tables and dotted keys land with a later block?
system_choice: Rejected as syntax errors in this block; only top-level key = string pairs are decoded. The string slice needs no more than that. Is that acceptable, or should tables and dotted keys land with a later block?

title: Quoted keys
description: Basic and literal quoted keys are accepted, reusing the string parser. Bare keys are A-Za-z0-9, underscore, and dash. Is that acceptable?
system_choice: Basic and literal quoted keys are accepted, reusing the string parser. Bare keys are A-Za-z0-9, underscore, and dash. Is that acceptable?

title: Dotted key into a header-implied table
description: A dotted key that walks into a super-table created implicitly by a header (for example, [x.y.z], then [x], then y.w = 1) is rejected. The spec says dotted keys may not touch tables already created, and the suite passes. Is that acceptable, or should it change on replan?
system_choice: A dotted key that walks into a super-table created implicitly by a header (for example, [x.y.z], then [x], then y.w = 1) is rejected. The spec says dotted keys may not touch tables already created, and the suite passes. Is that acceptable, or should it change on replan?
